reported_sequence: Sued in a separate debt case in what he recalls as a higher-level court
Received a large packet that appeared to be a printed spreadsheet
Recalls numbers and headings failing to align across pages
Asked opposing counsel to explain the packet
Recalls receiving no satisfactory explanation and no expectation from the court that counsel would provide the explanation he sought
Clarifies that the judge instructed him to subpoena the creator and described that person as the only one able to explain the records
personal_account.reported_expectation: Assumed a lawyer offering records accepted by the court could explain them
unknowns: Court, jurisdiction, judge, case date, docket, and claimant

personal_account.reported_judicial_instruction: Rigler recalls that the judge said he should have subpoenaed the records' creator and that the creator was the only person who could explain them; no transcript supplied.
personal_account.question_raised: Whether a creator's death or unavailability would invalidate records that remain accepted while further explanation is inaccessible

research_limitations: Texas sources are contextual comparisons pending identification of the court and case date
